boundary_evidence.start: TheBoot starts at $400986 with the executable boot-block version test. It follows system initialization owned by the adjacent startup module.
boundary_evidence.end: SetDefaultFolder ends with RTS at $400C74. The next span starts at $400C76 with the file-system initialization entry.
boundary_evidence.released_offsets: Boot1.a lines 219 through 237 retain the Mac Plus AfterInitResources offset $0A44 and ReBoot offset $0B82. Both match this module.

edits.description: Restored the Mac Plus boot flow from TheBoot through SetDefaultFolder. The evidence records 60 matching released operations and 185 ROM-only operations. All 752 emitted bytes are instructions.

Restored the older executable boot-block version test, heap selection, startup bitmap, DSAT resource zero, second-page reservation, debugger loading, INIT IDs zero through 35, and startup application fallback.

Restored the older loader interface: D3 selects the destination and header handling, A1 returns the loaded address, D4 holds the byte count, and D0 returns status. Positive mode loads the entire file at $800(A6), zero mode skips 512 bytes and loads below BufPtr, and negative mode skips 512 bytes and allocates a pointer.
Retained the write to ioRefNum(SP) at $400B14. Also retained the negative loader mode behavior that leaves D2 zero after a successful NewPtr: a later read error still returns success.

Used the released trap names for their exact opcodes, including InitApplZone at $A02C and RDrvrInstall at $A04F. NewHandleSysClear and PurgeMemSys add the documented system-heap and clear flags to their base trap words.

Retained released headers, early boot history, matching operation comments, loader comments, boot register interface, and the MacsBug six-byte return adjustment contract. Omitted the later claim that boot alert numbers must be negative and the obsolete claim that bb128KSHeap is unused. The source identifies restored bodies as reconstruction notes.

preceding_comments: ; Load the MacsBug debugger, and optionally the other debug thing (Disassembler).
; If there is no MacsBug, no attempt is made to load Disassmbler.
; Before loading MacsBug (below BufPtr), 1024 bytes of globals are reserved.
; MacsBug and the Disassembler are responsible for lowering BufPtr themselves after being loaded.
; If they don’t, they will be overwritten by the stack and globals of the first application.
; NOTE: the following code must not change in length - MacsBug depends upon it (blegh!)
; If MacsBug punts, it adds the magic offset 6 (bytes, that is) to the return address
; to skip over this code.  Ideally, the interface should allow the debugger to return
; an error code (in, say, D0?) to allow happy bypassing of this message.

verification.method: Called the shared verify_module function in an independent temporary directory. It assembled the source, linked at the ROM address, checked entry points and relocations, and compared every emitted byte.
verification.scope: The entire emitted span matches the ROM. MPW assembly has not been run. Byte equality does not establish original formatting or original names for reconstructed labels.
